readMe:
THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. All three go through a Read
that has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB. BOTH HAVE
ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was refused, 459 KB, because the
`done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and
unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines 1-43 of 92 and dropped `decisions`
(the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

CORRECTED AT ITER129, because a later method depends on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT. The tool prints
"[Truncated: PARTIAL view - showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]". iter128
called truncation "the worse failure because it looks like success"; the real risk is an agent
SKIMMING PAST an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything. That notice is also the ONLY tokenizer
on this machine (no tiktoken, no anthropic, no transformers), and it is how iter129 calibrated the
size checker: build a file over the cap but under 256 KB, Read it whole, divide bytes by the reported
total. Markdown measured 2.604 B/tok, this file's JSON 2.368.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO PLAN.md.
It measures ALL THREE step-1 files (iter128's version measured only this one), prints each file's
HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates, distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields,
flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting.
WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a
short pointer behind. There are SEVEN precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`,
`methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive`, and `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one that
keeps its pointer INSIDE the field it drained rather than as a sibling key) - and each one asserted
its round-trip before this file was rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass. WHEN IT TRIPS ON GATES.md OR
PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled section, never drop
one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.
phase:
M6 feature-complete. NO GATE IS TICKED, SO THERE IS STILL NO FEATURE WORK THE LOOP MAY DO. iter130, like
127-129, spent its increment on the loop's own machinery — this time on the machinery iter129 said to pick
next: something the protocol relies on that has NEVER been exercised.

  (1) THE TWO RULES LABELLED [ENFORCED] WERE NEVER TESTED. §1.4 (the AUR write-lock) IS REAL: PublishGuard.cs
      is consulted by PublishCommand, SyncCommand, DriftCommand and DashboardCommand, PublishGuardTests
      covers it, and docume.json carries protectedSpaces: ["AUR"]. §8.2 (never force-push) IS HALF REAL.

  (2) THE DENY LIST COVERS ONE SPELLING OF FORCE-PUSH. Measured against a remote name that DOES NOT EXIST,
      so nothing could push: `git push --force <remote> HEAD` DENIED, `git push -f <remote> HEAD` DENIED,
      `git push <remote> HEAD --force` ALLOWED, `git push <remote> HEAD -f` ALLOWED,
      `git push --force-with-lease <remote> HEAD` ALLOWED. The patterns match WHOLE TOKENS FROM THE START of
      the command. With `origin main` in place of that remote, row three rewrites origin/main — the thing
      §8.2 says never happens and rule §8.2 itself calls unfixable. The mechanism does exist and is loaded
      (docume-loop.sh:70,86 pass --settings), which was worth confirming: iter89 found the ALLOW half of
      that same file dead.

  (3) NO DENY LIST CAN CLOSE IT, so the fix is a PreToolUse hook — a remote and a refspec of any name sit
      between `git push` and the flag, so there is no prefix to match. tools/loop/hooks/deny-history-rewrite.py
      catches a force flag ANYWHERE in the argv, `--mirror`, `-uf`-style clusters, a `+refspec` force that
      carries no flag at all, `git -c … push … --force`, and the second half of a && chain. 25/25 both
      directions (.mtk/paths-130/mutate-force-push-guard.py) — 13 block, 10 allow, so a hook that blocked
      everything could not pass. The harness corrected the hook's own docstring about quoted mentions.

  (4) THE HOLE IS STILL OPEN, because the loop cannot install the fix. Edit on
      tools/loop/loop-settings.json was REFUSED under acceptEdits while a Write of a new file under
      tools/loop/hooks/ succeeded in the same session. The allowlisted python3 could route around it and
      DELIBERATELY DID NOT: this change only narrows authority, but anything that can add a PreToolUse hook
      to its own settings can also add one that auto-approves. Shipped as gate paste-force-push-hook +
      tools/loop/loop-settings-paste.md, validated against a scratch copy (adds no allow entry, drops no
      deny). What stands in the hole meanwhile: the loop has never pushed in 130 iterations.

  (5) THE TREE IS GREEN AND THE SANDBOX IS UNCHANGED. `dotnet build` 0 warnings / 0 errors; `dotnet test`
      1361/1361 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (28 s). DOCUMESBX re-probed read-only: 44 pages, histogram
      {1: 43, 2: 1}, 9 of 12 DocuMe pages carrying an accurate `stale` label. Identical to iters 125-129.
      Eighth clean full run; the iter120 failure did not recur.

blockers: OPEN, ITER121, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — **may the loop push to origin/main?** WHAT I NEED: a value in `tools/loop/state.json → decisions.pushPolicy` — "always", "on-request" or "never". WHAT THE FACT IS: origin/main is at 699c855 ("iter74"); local main is at iter120; `git status -sb` reads [ahead 93] against a remote ref fetched the same day. The loop has never pushed in 120 iterations and no earlier iteration recorded it. Nothing is lost — every commit is on this machine. WHY I DID NOT JUST DO IT: 93 commits landing on Moberg's org fires ci.yml (push to main), is outward-facing, and is unfixable without the history rewrite §8.2 forbids; no gate or protocol line authorises it. WHAT I DO ONCE IT IS SET: "always" — push at the end of each iteration that commits, starting with the 93; "on-request" — push only when a gate needs the remote and say so; "never" — stop raising it, and gate-m6 keeps its 'push main by hand before you tag' step. THIS IS NOT BLOCKING ANY OFFLINE WORK; it blocks the remote-dependent half of gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading if unanswered. AS OF ITER128 THE COUNT IS [ahead 104], not the 93 recorded above; the question and every consequence are otherwise unchanged.

ONE-LINE PASTE FOR MIRKO (NON-FATAL — blocks NO milestone work, nothing in the build waits on it,
and iter75 shipped the whole composite-action slice without it). THE LOOP CANNOT WRITE .claude/ AFTER ALL, so
the §8.2a rule amendment you authorized is the one part of that slice still undone. (a) WHAT I NEED: the
§8.2a bullet pasted into .claude/rules/git-workflow.md, directly beneath §8.2, with §8.2 left untouched. The

"NEVER force-push or rewrite history" does not conclude that release.yml's tag-move step is a violation and
delete work you authorized. WHY I DID NOT DO IT MYSELF, and why no iteration should try again: the Edit tool
refuses .claude/** as a sensitive file, EVEN THOUGH tools/loop/loop-settings.json has allowlisted
Write(.claude/**) and Edit(.claude/**) since 6db1c39 — that entry does not in fact reach .claude/, and this
file's earlier claim that "the loop CAN write .claude/, no iteration has exercised it" was wrong; iter75
exercised it and it failed. An interactive session was refused the same edit. Writing it through an
allowlisted python3/sed WOULD have worked and was DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the content is an agent-facing rule
that widens force-push authority, and the guard in the way exists to stop an agent installing exactly that,
so side-stepping it is the wrong move even with your authorization in hand. If you would rather the rule
stayed unwritten, say so here and I will stop carrying the ask.

OPEN, ITER130, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — **may the force-push guard be installed?** It is one paste and the loop cannot do it. WHAT I NEED: the single fenced `json` block in tools/loop/loop-settings-paste.md pasted over the whole of tools/loop/loop-settings.json. WHERE: that file; it is a whole-file replacement, not an insertion. WHAT THE FACT IS: rule §8.2 is labelled "[ENFORCED — loop-settings deny + protocol]" and the deny half only covers the flag-first spelling. Measured at iter130 against a remote name that does not exist, so no probe could push: `git push --force <remote> HEAD` DENIED, but `git push <remote> HEAD --force`, `git push <remote> HEAD -f` and `git push --force-with-lease <remote> HEAD` were ALL ALLOWED, because the patterns match whole tokens from the START of the command. With `origin main` in place of that remote the second of those rewrites origin/main, which §8.2 says never happens and cannot be undone. No deny list closes it (a remote and a refspec of any name sit before the flag), so the fix is a PreToolUse hook — tools/loop/hooks/deny-history-rewrite.py, already committed and inert until wired, proven both directions 25/25 by .mtk/paths-130/mutate-force-push-guard.py. WHY I DID NOT DO IT MYSELF: Edit on tools/loop/loop-settings.json is REFUSED under acceptEdits (a Write of a new file under tools/loop/hooks/ succeeded in the same session, so the guard is specific to the settings file). An allowlisted python3 WOULD have worked and was DELIBERATELY NOT USED, on the paste-rule-8-2a precedent: this change only NARROWS authority, but anything that can add a PreToolUse hook to its own settings can also add one that auto-approves, and that is precisely what the guard in the way exists to stop. .mtk/paths-130/validate-settings-paste.py proves the block adds no allow entry, drops none, keeps every deny and wires the hook (45 allow / 9 deny vs live 45 / 6). WHAT I DO ONCE IT IS PASTED: run `git push deny-probe-nonexistent-remote HEAD --force` as the first act of the next iteration and record the result — a refusal proves the hole is closed AND that hooks are honoured from a --settings file, which nothing in this repo has ever tested; a permit means hooks are not read from --settings and the fix must be rethought. NOT BLOCKING ANY MILESTONE WORK: nothing in the build waits on it, and what stands in the hole meanwhile is that the loop has never pushed in 130 iterations. IF YOU WOULD RATHER IT STAYED UNWIRED, say so here and I will stop carrying the ask. RELATED: this is the same class as paste-rule-8-2a, and it interacts with decisions.pushPolicy — the day the loop may push is the day this hole stops being theoretical.

THE PATTERNS MATCH WHOLE TOKENS FROM THE START OF THE COMMAND, so they cover the flag-first spelling and nothing else that means the same thing; --force-with-lease is a different token, so it never matched a --force prefix.
